title: Mara and the Lantern
premise: In the winter of 1893, Hazel Nystrom keeps the light at Gullwrack Point, the last inhabited place before the river freezes and the bridge closes. When a half-drowned stranger washes ashore carrying her late husband's stolen ledger — proof that the shipping company's negligence drowned eleven men, including her brother-in-law — Hazel must decide whether to expose the truth or protect the family that depends on the company's wages. As the ice thickens and the town turns on itself, she discovers the stranger is her husband's illegitimate son, and the berth on the last boat out can hold only one of them. In the end, Hazel sends the boy away with the ledger and stays to face the magistrate herself, choosing justice over safety and finding that memory, like the light, must be tended by someone who remains.
about_author: Quentin Kavanagh is the pen name of a former Great Lakes merchant marine who spent a decade researching lighthouse keepers' logs from the 1890s. He writes from a converted pilot house on Lake Superior, where he claims the fog still tells him stories.

chapters.title: The Last Boat Before Ice
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. She trims the lamp and watches the final ferry carry the season's last travelers across, noting which townsfolk stayed behind and why. Her daughter Mara begs to leave with them; Hazel refuses, hiding her fear of the closed bridge. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: What the River Gives Back
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A body washes into the cove — alive, barely. She drags the young man inside, finds a leather ledger wrapped in oilskin against his chest. He murmurs a name she hasn't spoken in fifteen years: her husband's. Beat: shock cracking open old grief.

chapters.title: Silences I Have Kept
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Hazel's POV. Fifteen years earlier: her husband Elias's mysterious trips downriver, his death ruled accidental, her choice not to ask questions. The chapter reveals how carefully she learned to keep people safe by keeping quiet. Beat: guilt surfacing.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Knows My Husband's Face
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Hazel and the stranger, Tomas. He recovers enough to explain: Elias was his father; the ledger records the Meridian Shipping Company knowingly sending an overloaded, unseaworthy barge out in a storm. Eleven men drowned. Beat: inheritance of a dangerous truth.

chapters.title: Mara Finds the Ledger
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Curious and resentful of her mother's secrecy, Mara reads the ledger while Hazel sleeps. She recognizes her uncle Alden's name among the dead — the man whose wages kept them fed. Beat: betrayal arriving through paper.

chapters.title: Alden's Widow Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Ruth, Alden's widow, arrives snowbound, desperate for word about a pension the company promised. Hazel lies badly. Ruth notices the bandages drying by the stove. Beat: the cost of silence made visible in another woman's face.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. News comes by signal flag: ice has taken the bridge; no one crosses until spring thaw. Tomas panics — the company's agents will come for the ledger when the river freezes solid enough to walk. Beat: claustrophobia, the trap closing.

chapters.title: Company Men
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Two agents arrive 'to inspect the light,' asking pointed questions about wreckage and survivors. Hazel performs the competent, incurious keeper. After they leave, she finds they've searched her stores. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Which Silences Keep People Safe
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mother and daughter clash over the ledger: Mara wants it burned, Hazel wants it read aloud. Mara accuses her mother of choosing dead men over living ones. Beat: the theme argued in a kitchen, love strained by principle.

chapters.title: Ruth's Testimony
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Ruth returns, having guessed everything, and instead of betraying them offers what she knows: the night of the wreck, a company clerk weeping in her kitchen, a second copy of the manifest hidden in the church records. Beat: grief becoming alliance.

chapters.title: Walking on the Frozen River
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The agents cross the ice on foot with lanterns, hunting the survivor. Hazel hides Tomas in the lamp room; the light itself becomes cover. Beat: terror under the turning beam, the keeper's craft weaponized.

chapters.title: The Manifest in the Church
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. She and Ruth retrieve the second manifest from behind the church register during a blizzard service. The sexton sees them and says nothing — another silence, this one chosen kindly. Beat: solidarity among the overlooked.

chapters.title: A Name for the Boy
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Hazel finally calls him by name and tells him about his father honestly — including Elias's cowardice in signing the false manifest. Tomas rages, then grieves. Beat: inheritance without illusion; forgiveness beginning.

chapters.title: The Agents Return with Warrants
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The agents return with papers naming Tomas a thief and Hazel an accessory. They seize the light's stores as leverage. Mara, terrified, nearly hands over the ledger. Beat: the law arriving as an instrument of the guilty.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs in short sections. The women of the point organize: Ruth copies the documents, the sexton hides the originals, fishermen agree to testify when the ice breaks. Hazel realizes the case cannot wait for a court that the company owns. Beat: community as tribunal.

chapters.title: The Thaw Begins
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Cracks sing across the river; the first boat of spring is announced — one berth, secured by Hazel months ago, before anyone knew what the winter would hold. Only one of them can leave to carry the evidence to the federal court in the city. Beat: hope and impossible arithmetic.

chapters.title: Mara Demands the Berth
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara argues she should go: she's young, fast, unknown to the agents. Hazel refuses — the company knows Mara's face from summer visits. The fight turns cruel and true. Beat: motherhood tested against strategy.

chapters.title: The Night Walk
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The agents attempt to burn the boathouse and the ledger with it. Hazel saves the documents but burns her hand badly; Tomas pulls her from the fire. The town sees the agents do it. Beat: the villains unmask themselves.

chapters.title: Which Family Member Gets the Berth
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The climax of decision: Hazel puts the choice to the family council — Ruth, Mara, Tomas, the sexton. She rules that Tomas must go: he is the witness, the son, the one the law will listen to. Mara must stay and keep the light with her. Beat: sacrifice named aloud.

chapters.title: Ice Breaks
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The last-berth boat fights the breaking ice; agents pursue along the shore. Hazel works the lamp in daylight, burning it bright to blind their aim and mark the channel. Tomas escapes with the ledger. Beat: the light as defiance.

chapters.title: The Magistrate Comes to the Point
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Spring brings not punishment but a federal inquiry; Tomas's testimony lands. The company men are arrested; Ruth receives her pension and an apology read aloud in the church. Hazel testifies about fifteen years of silences. Beat: reckoning, imperfect but real.

chapters.title: Mara and the Lantern
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, closing frame. Mara, now apprentice keeper, lights the lamp beside her mother and understands the inheritance: not the ledger, not the name, but the tending. Tomas's letters arrive by the first ferry. Beat: memory kept alight, the future lit by it.
